input.quote: On and after the Closing Date or Acquisition Date, as applicable, until a Receivable has been paid in full, acquired or sold to a third party under Section 3.4, the Servicer will mark its receivables systems to indicate clearly that the Receivable is owned by the Issuer and has been pledged to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture.
input.rationale: Direction of ownership runs in our favour throughout. Section 2.1(a)/(b) has the Depositor "transfer and absolutely assign to the Issuer... all of the Depositor's right, title and interest" in the Receivables and related Depositor Transferred Property; Section 9.2 bars any further transfer or Lien; Section 9.4(a) requires Cellco to flag its own receivables systems to show the Receivables are owned by the Issuer; and Section 3.10(b) has the Custodian hold the Receivable Files "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee", with Section 7.5(b) requiring delivery of the Receivable Files and the accounts and records to a Successor Servicer. Nothing assigns our property, records or obligor data to Cellco, and no joint ownership is created, so there is no walk-away exposure. This is a securitisation transfer and servicing agreement rather than a procurement contract, so there is no classic deliverables/work-product IP clause; the only counterparty-favourable carve-out is Section 7.5(b), under which the Servicer "will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications" — that is Cellco retaining its own platform, tools and know-how, which the playbook expressly permits and which sits at the fallback position (vendor keeps generic tools; we keep the files, records and data we own). We note in passing the absence of an express licence-back of servicing software or systems to support a servicing transition, which is a sub-element short of the preferred position but not a material failure warranting a redline here.
